title: US retail and food services sales (advance), October 2026
made_at_note: evidence.json, which holds the forecast, was written at this time (UTC)
sealed_at_note: written by our own machine; the independent date is the OpenTimestamps proof census-retail-sales-2026-10-seal.json.ots
code_note: the commit of the private code repository that built the seal and the one that ran the evidence; the seal's numbers recompute from its inputs either way

series.name: Advance retail sales: retail trade and food services
series.units: millions of dollars (not adjusted for prices)

target.release_basis: announced: https://www.census.gov/economic-indicators/calendar-listview-2026.html ('November 17, 2026 8:30 AM Advance Monthly Sales for Retail and Food Services October 2026')

vintage.note: The advance estimate is revised with the November release (2026-12-16, announced) and in annual revisions.

notes: The headline is the percent change from September; it follows from the sealed level and September's value as printed on release day.
claim_rule: 'sealed before publication' only if the OpenTimestamps attestation's block time precedes the release; a seal attested on or after the release is void

forecast.units: millions of dollars (not adjusted for prices)

selection.rule: Serve the method with the lowest out-of-time MAE over the backtest origins. Where the ensemble's MAE gap to that method has a 95% interval (moving-block bootstrap of origins) that holds zero, serve the ensemble. If the method served is the random walk, the target is not sealed: the model adds nothing over repeating the last value.
selection.basis: drift has the lowest MAE; the ensemble's gap to it, +155.803 (95% interval -20.713 to +359.627), holds zero

method.selection_rule: Serve the method with the lowest out-of-time MAE over the backtest origins. Where the ensemble's MAE gap to that method has a 95% interval (moving-block bootstrap of origins) that holds zero, serve the ensemble. If the method served is the random walk, the target is not sealed: the model adds nothing over repeating the last value.

point.seasonal_naive: the value one season before the target
point.drift: the last value plus h times the mean change over the fit window
point.ets: damped-trend exponential smoothing, weights from a fixed grid by the least in-sample one-step squared error
point.ensemble_mean: the mean of random_walk, drift, ets on the log scale (a geometric mean)

method.bands: split-conformal, every method its own: the point plus or minus the ceil((n+1)*level)-th smallest absolute 1-step-ahead residual of that method over its newest 60 rolling-origin backtest origins, on the log scale

scoring_plan: Target: Advance retail sales: retail trade and food services (RSAFS), 2026-10, as published by U.S. Census Bureau and read from https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=RSAFS.

Value scored against: the first print: the value U.S. Census Bureau publishes for 2026-10 on release day, read from the spec's URL on or after the release and before 2026-12-16, when the next release may revise it. The scorer records the value, the retrieval time and the sha256 of the raw response. Vintage note: The advance estimate is revised with the November release (2026-12-16, announced) and in annual revisions.
Not scored, with the reason, if the period is not published by 2027-05-18, if it was published before this seal's OpenTimestamps attestation, or if the series is redefined.

Metric: absolute error in millions of dollars (not adjusted for prices) for the served forecast (ensemble_mean, the headline) and for every other sealed method, the three baselines (random walk, seasonal naive, drift) among them; whether the published value falls inside each method's sealed 80% and 95% bands; the interval score at both levels. Published to 0 decimal place(s), so the published value carries up to half a unit of rounding in its last place.
Claim: 'sealed before publication' when the attestation's block time precedes the release.
